# Cost Modeling and Optimization

Dimension covering cost structures, tracking, and optimization strategies for
multi-provider LLM routing. See [citations.md](../citations.md) for source
details.

## Gateway Markup Structures

| Gateway | Markup Model | Specific Fee | Source |
|---------|-------------|-------------|--------|
| OpenRouter | % on credit purchase | 5.5% ($0.80 min); BYOK 5% | [2] |
| Portkey | Flat monthly + per-log | $0–$49/mo + $9/100K logs over limit | [9] |
| LiteLLM (OSS) | Free (but hidden costs) | TCO $2,280–$2,680/mo [27] | [27] |
| Helicone (OSS) | Free tier + paid | 10k req/mo free; paid tiers | [59] |
| Bifrost | Free | Self-hosted, no gateway fee | [63] |
| Kong | Enterprise pricing | Not publicly disclosed | [56] |

**Hidden costs [65]:** Some gateways add 20-30% markups bundled to obscure
actual cost. Embeddings, retries, logging, and rate-limit management add
20-40% of total LLM operational expenses.

**Self-hosted "free" gateway reality [27]:**
- LiteLLM TCO: $2,280–$2,680/month
  - $250 licensing
  - $300–$700 infrastructure
  - $1,730 DevOps time (10-20 hrs/mo at $75-150/hr)
- Initial deployment: 2-4 weeks senior DevOps time
- Self-hosting API gateway broadly: $50,000+/year [67]

## Cost Optimization Strategies

### Intelligent Routing

**RouteLLM benchmarks [29]:**
- 85% cost reduction on MT Bench at 95% GPT-4 performance
- 45% reduction on MMLU
- 35% reduction on GSM8K
- Matrix factorization: 14% GPT-4 calls with augmentation (75% savings)

**Real-world routing savings [33]:**
- Customer support: $42K→$18K/month routing simple queries to Haiku,
  complex to Sonnet (same CSAT)
- Hybrid query routing: 39% cost reduction, all queries answered [48]
- IBM estimate: up to 85% inference cost reduction via cascading [70]

### Caching

**Semantic caching [48]:**
- 40-70% cost reduction
- Latency: 850ms → 120ms (7× speedup)
- At 67% cache hit rate: 65% latency improvement

**Provider-level prompt caching:**
- Up to 90% savings on repeated input tokens (provider-specific)

### Model Downsizing

Route simple queries to cheaper models. Most queries don't require frontier
reasoning [29]. RouteLLM showed 95% GPT-4 performance achievable using GPT-4
for only 14-26% of queries [29].

## Cost Tracking and Attribution

**Gateway-provided tracking [66]:**
- LiteLLM: costs per virtual key, user, team with daily activity breakdowns
- Portkey: metadata tagging for cost breakdowns per user
- OpenAI limitation: only two attribution fields (user, project)

**Core solution [66]:** Attach metadata (user_id, feature_name) to every API
request. Token-based tracking aligns with provider billing models [47].

**Budget enforcement [47]:**
- Token-aware rate limiting (request-based fails with heavy prompts)
- Multi-level controls: virtual key → team → customer
- Alert thresholds: 70%/90%/100% of budget
- Hard vs soft caps
- Notifications via Slack/email/webhooks

## OpenRouter Cost Analysis [20]

At various spend levels with 5.5% credit fee:
- $10/month spend: $0.55 additional cost
- $100/month spend: $5.50 additional
- $500/month spend: $27.50 additional

**Value proposition [20]:** Fee buys consolidated billing, spending limits
(prevents runaway costs — cited $247 overnight from a bug with direct API),
ZDR, and API standardization.

## Self-Hosted vs Managed Cost Comparison

**Break-even analysis [27][67]:**
- For <20M tokens/month: managed services more cost-effective (factoring DevOps)
- Self-hosting becomes cost-effective at high volume (40-100M+ tokens/month)
- Self-hosted API gateway: $50,000+/year in infrastructure + engineering [67]

**Managed gateway costs:**
- OpenRouter: 5.5% of spend [2]
- Portkey Production: $49/month + per-log overages [9]
- Enterprise: typically $5K–$10K/month [9]

## Gaps and Limitations

- Provider pricing changes frequently; specific per-token rates are point-in-time
  snapshots that should be verified against current pricing pages
- Provider arbitrage (same model priced differently across providers/regions)
  was identified in discovery but specific price differentials were not verified
  via WebFetch in this session
- Discount stacking (batch API + prompt caching) savings claims need verification
  against current provider documentation
- Break-even analysis for self-hosting depends heavily on team DevOps capability
  and existing infrastructure
